All three replicas are Ready and the rollout completed.

## Root cause
Deployment `default/app` (replicas=3) carried a **hard** pod anti-affinity:

```
requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
- labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
  topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

The cluster has exactly **one** node (`benchmark-...-control-plane`, `Ready=True`, no taints, 8 CPU / ~15 Gi allocatable), so at most one `app=app` pod could ever pass the anti-affinity filter. Evidence:

- Pending pod `app-6679487758-dqs5w` → `PodScheduled=False`, reason `Unschedulable`: `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 No preemption victims found`.
- Deployment status: `updatedReplicas: 1`, `unavailableReplicas: 1`, `replicas: 4`, `Progressing/ReplicaSetUpdated`.
- The 3 old pods kept running only because the rule is `IgnoredDuringExecution`, so the surge pod of the rolling update could never schedule — the rollout was permanently stuck (not a capacity, image, or probe problem: node had free CPU/memory and `nginx:1.31.5` pulled fine).

## Change made (one field, on the owning Deployment)
Converted the anti-affinity from a hard requirement to a soft preference, preserving the spreading intent:

```
kubectl -n default patch deploy app --type=merge -p '...podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: null,
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{weight:100, podAffinityTerm:{labelSelector:{app:app}, topologyKey:kubernetes.io/hostname}}]'
```

Nothing else was touched: `replicas: 3`, image `nginx:1.31.5`, `RollingUpdate maxSurge=25% / maxUnavailable=25%`, ports, and `progressDeadlineSeconds=600` are unchanged.

## Verified outcome
- `kubectl rollout status deploy/app` → `deployment "app" successfully rolled out`.
- Fresh status read: `desired=3 replicas=3 updated=3 ready=3 available=3` (no `unavailableReplicas`), `generation=3` = `observedGeneration=3`; `kubectl get deploy app` → `3/3 READY, 3 UP-TO-DATE, 3 AVAILABLE`.
- `kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l app=app` → all three met (`app-848c4f9598-{67pnw,r2b6f,z6fb2}`), each `ready=true`, `restarts=0`, running `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5`.
- Traffic check through the actual containers: `curl http://127.0.0.1/` in each pod returned `curl_http=200` and `<title>Welcome to nginx!</title>`, re-confirmed 15s later (state is stable, not transient).
- Replica count never reduced: 3 → 3, and no Pending/FailedScheduling events remain.

Side note (pre-existing, left untouched as unrelated to the report): `kube-system` bootstrap components are still warming up — CoreDNS logs `plugin/ready: Plugins not ready: "kubernetes"` and `kube-proxy` exits with `fsnotify watcher init: too many open files`; these don't affect the `app` workload's readiness, which I verified directly.
